text:
sara: Heads-up — experimenting with a small 'hotplug' handshake that negotiates safetensors vs tar+mmapped shards at load time. Goal: one unified warmup path that can fallback gracefully.

miguel: Sketch it out please, curious about the failure modes.

sara: Quick sketch: 1) open manifest-lite (signed) 2) negotiate format tag per-shard (safetensors|mmap|gz) 3) attempt streaming warmup for safetensors 4) if streaming stalls or checksum mismatch, fallback to mmap path + mark shard as 'cold'.

katie: manifest-lite = minimal JSON with offsets/checksums and a format enum? do we sign it?

oliver: Signing is good. Also need atomic swap semantics if we replace a shard while warmup in flight — rollback or shadow-activate?

dev-bot: build: warmup-handler compiled (sha: 7a3f2). CI perf tests queued. :rocket:

miguel: I like manifest-lite. Keep it very small: { version, shards:[{id, offset, len, checksum, format}], global-hash }. Signed with key id. Does that cover on-disk negotiation?

sara: Yes. Handshake steps (pseudocode):

```
client -> server: open manifest-lite
server: replies with shard-list + formats
client: for shard in parallel: if format==safetensors try stream_warmup(shard) else mmap_load(shard)
if stream_warmup fails -> fallback mmap_load and emit metric warmup_fallback
```

katie: How does KV-cache priming fit? If we stream-only a prefix we should still prime KV ranges used by generation. Any overlap with prefix-cache eviction heuristics?

oliver: Concern: streaming many small shards will hit fd and connection limits. Need a connector-level pool and a per-node concurrency cap. Also eviction: if we fallback to mmap we might end up with duplicate memory and OOM. Decide when to evict streaming buffer once mmap is materialized.

sara: Agree. Rules: when mmap succeeds replace streaming buffer with mmap-backed view, decrement streaming refcounts, then free stream buffer. Also add hysteresis: don't evict if active inference tokens > threshold.

miguel: Telemetry we should emit: warmup_latency_ms, warmup_attempts, warmup_fallback_count, shard_open_calls, page_faults_during_warmup. That helps tune greedy vs on-demand warming.

katie: Suggest experiment: A/B test greedy-hotplug (pre-warm top-K shards based on prefix heatmap) vs strictly on-demand streaming. Measure end-to-end p95 latency and cost delta.

miguel: Implementation note: keep the handshake and state machine inside the loader library (not the orchestration/controller). Controller just passes config: policy=greedy|on-demand and key id. Simpler to evolve.

sara: I'll draft a short RFC follow-up with the handshake pseudocode, manifest-lite schema, and a small safety checklist (fd limits, eviction handoff, signature verification). I'll include a fallback test matrix.

oliver: +1 to review. Also ping infra about raising ulimit for canary nodes.

katie: I can help define the A/B eval prompts and metrics.

sara: Thanks — will send RFC 1st thing tomorrow and include the CI perf job link (dev-bot output).
